title: Alvin Roth to the rescue, the polity that is Singapore - Marginal REVOLUTION
gist: Singapore's GovTech has piloted FirstDate, a government dating app for public-sector employees aged 21-35 that uses a Nobel-winning matching algorithm and gives one match at a time, as the latest state effort to reverse fast-falling fertility.

insights.claim: Singapore launched FirstDate, a government dating platform piloted for public-sector employees aged 21-35, as a social-engineering experiment to tackle its fast-declining fertility rate.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Shows how far governments in rapidly aging economies are willing to go to intervene in family formation.
insights.quote: the latest social-engineering experiment by the city-state’s government to tackle its fast-declining fertility rate
insights.locator: Singapore has launched a dating platform

insights.claim: Singapore's falling birth rate has made it one of the world's fastest-ageing countries, prompting repeated government efforts to reverse it.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Demographic aging is a structural macro headwind (labor force, fiscal) driving policy experimentation.
insights.locator: The app, which joins a crowded

insights.claim: FirstDate uses a Nobel Economics Prize-winning matchmaking algorithm and gives users only one match at a time, plus a tool suggesting date activities and a post-date survey.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Applying stable-matching market design to dating is a live test of whether fewer, better-matched options outperform swipe-based abundance.
insights.quote: uses a Nobel Economics Prize-winning matchmaking algorithm

insights.claim: The app's founding question was whether having more potential matches actually makes it easier to find a suitable match — implicitly challenging the choice-abundance model of commercial dating apps.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: If the one-match model works, it undercuts the engagement-maximizing design of incumbent dating platforms.
insights.quote: does having more potential matches necessarily make it easier to find a suitable match?

insights.claim: FirstDate came out of the annual hackathon run by Singapore government's technology agency (GovTech) and enters a crowded field of commercial dating apps and bespoke matchmaking services.
insights.speaker: Tyler Cowen
insights.so_what: Government entry into a crowded consumer-app market, though limited to a public-sector pilot for now.
